lines.text: Do you know how a match lights? The fire is split into two halves, and they only meet when you strike.
The match head holds a chemical packed with oxygen, mixed with sulfur and glue.
The strip on the box has red phosphorus and powdered glass.
Striking rubs a tiny bit of phosphorus into a hotter, touchier form. It catches fire in the air, and lights the head.
The stick is soaked in wax, so the flame keeps burning down the wood.
Orbi files burn out too. By default, 30 minutes after you send, the stored file is deleted. You can pick anything from five to thirty.
